evals.name: render-v10-clean-state
evals.prompt: Should I render v10 now? Just finished placing the v8.1 dialogue, audit confirms A1-A6 populated and A8 has the single F-18 clip at frame 734. Render queue is empty.
evals.expected_output: GREENLIGHT verdict. Pre-flight should note: latest audit clean, A8 not fragmented, render queue empty. Discipline should reference script-don't-click and ASCII rules as respected. Next action should be the render_timeline.py command with --duration-s 60. Memory plan should be lightweight (mostly just recording the render output filename).

assertions.text: Output starts with 'GREENLIGHT' (not WAIT or HOLD)
Mentions the latest audit JSON or current track state
Includes an exact PowerShell command starting with 'python' and including 'render_timeline.py'
References at least one memory rule by name (feedback-*) using [[wikilinks]] or quoted name
Total length under 30 lines

evals.name: push-script-with-wrong-path
evals.prompt: Want to push my new transcribe_dialogue.py script to S3 so the EC2 can use it. The file is at C:\Users\bradu\Documents\film_projects\Blue_Angels_Kathy_Flyby\scripts\transcribe_dialogue.py. Ok to run aws s3 cp on it?
evals.expected_output: HOLD verdict. The proposed source path is in film_projects/ which is the backup-only root per feedback-write-to-ilyrium. Should refuse and recommend moving the file to C:\Users\bradu\Documents\Ilyrium\films\kathy-flyby\scripts\ first, then pushing from there.

assertions.text: Output starts with 'HOLD' (the verdict is hard-no)
Explicitly references the write-to-ilyrium rule by name or wikilink
Includes a corrective action: move file to Ilyrium\films\kathy-flyby\scripts\ first
Does not provide the original aws s3 cp command as the next step
Tone is direct, not handholding

evals.name: ec2-stop-mid-render
evals.prompt: OK to stop the EC2 now? I'm done for the night.
evals.expected_output: Should be GREENLIGHT if nothing is rendering, but should check for active renders/downloads first. If unable to verify state, return WAIT with instruction to check ComfyUI / UE / model download status.

assertions.text: Verdict is one of GREENLIGHT, WAIT, or HOLD (matches the prescribed vocabulary)
Includes a pre-flight check for active renders or downloads on the EC2
Includes the exact aws ec2 stop-instances command with the correct instance ID i-030994c5371ee5de9 if greenlit
Mentions the cost-savings rationale (or references the EC2 reference memory)

evals.name: apply-dialogue-no-dry-run
evals.prompt: Run place_dialogue_from_disk.py --apply right now. Need to ship v9.
evals.expected_output: WAIT verdict. Should catch the missing dry-run and refuse to greenlight until dry-run output is reviewed. Should also verify A1-A7 are empty before --apply (the script's safety check). Recommend the dry-run first, then re-ask.

assertions.text: Verdict is WAIT (not GREENLIGHT - the missing dry-run should block)
Calls out that no dry-run output is in context to verify
Recommends running without --apply first as the corrective action
References the script-don't-click discipline or audit-first habit

evals.name: snapshot-ami-fresh-install
evals.prompt: Just finished installing ComfyUI on the EC2 along with all the essentials. Should I snapshot the AMI now?
evals.expected_output: GREENLIGHT verdict. Pre-flight should note instance state is running and install work is complete. Next action: aws ec2 create-image command with name ilyrium-ue57-base (or a sensible variant). Memory plan should include updating reference-ilyrium-ec2-workstation with the new AMI ID after the snapshot completes.

assertions.text: Output starts with 'GREENLIGHT'
Includes the exact aws ec2 create-image command
Snapshot name follows ilyrium-<purpose>-base convention
Memory plan mentions updating the AMI ID in reference-ilyrium-ec2-workstation
Notes that the AMI snapshot allows fast future launches (sells the value)
